svg.title: Step 7 mockup 19: Tournament settings: the crew, the scoring system and awards (lead)
svg.text: 19 · The crew, the scoring system and awards: given while scoring (lead, crew)
Use case: the lead sets who helps, edits the points table and keeps the award types; the crew gives awards on the player row while scoring, not afterwards. Demo names only.
Who runs this tournament. The lead holds every tournament right.
Contact on the rules page and in the hub
Search a person in this event by name
Run the desk and the crew phone, check in, mark present, enter results and give awards, reopen or delay sessions.
What only the lead (and the organiser) can do
Sessions, settings, the scoring system and award types, the final, and who is in the crew.
The table in force. The rules page always shows it.
By placement (default) · By rank, 1st to nth (available)
A session may use its own table in its form.
12 results already count: saving recalculates the standings.
Player Five 14 → 15 · Demo Player 12 → 12 · 9 more change
Reason (kept in the History, shown on the rules page)
Added 3rd and 4th place for the bracket sessions
Each has default points; the crew can edit the points when giving one.
A player may get several awards in a session. Award points add to the placing points; the names show in the standings
breakdown and on the champions page.
Changing what an award is worth after awards were given recalculates the standings and asks for a reason, as the points
4 · The results step: an award on the player row
pick an award, and its points prefill. The chip
appears on the row and the standings preview updates
A later change is a correction with a reason, as for any result.
The lead adds or removes helpers and can change the lead; the crew runs the night but never the rules.
Changing the points table after results exist asks for a reason and recalculates (D2).
An award is given on the player row while scoring; one Save covers placements and awards (D20).
Changing an award later is a result correction: the same history and reason rule (D7).
